name: Japanese
intro: Learn hiragana, katakana and kanji with readings in whole words. Kana transcribe morae rather than English-style syllables; long vowels, small っ and ん affect timing. Pitch accent varies by region and needs audio. Standard Japanese is the main model. Romanisation is an initial aid; professional reading requires kanji and rapid sentence processing.

foundation.name: Japanese
notes: Hiragana writes grammar endings and many ordinary words. Katakana writes many loanwords, names and emphasis. Kanji are characters with meanings and context-dependent readings. The table contains the 46 basic hiragana and their katakana partners; this is a syllabary, not an English-style alphabet.

Dakuten ゛ gives forms such as か→が, さ→ざ, た→だ, は→ば. Handakuten ゜ gives は→ぱ. Small ゃ/ゅ/ょ combine: きゃ = kya, one mora. Small っ marks a held consonant. Long vowels occupy an extra mora: おばさん = aunt; おばあさん = grandmother. Katakana often uses ー for length.

Topic は is pronounced wa, directional へ is e, and object を is o. Japanese r is usually a tap. Pitch accent differs by word and region; romaji does not show it. Learn recordings in context, then reduce dependence on romaji.

Voiced kana: が ぎ ぐ げ ご / ガ ギ グ ゲ ゴ; ざ じ ず ぜ ぞ / ザ ジ ズ ゼ ゾ; だ ぢ づ で ど / ダ ヂ ヅ デ ド; ば び ぶ べ ぼ / バ ビ ブ ベ ボ. Semi-voiced: ぱ ぴ ぷ ぺ ぽ / パ ピ プ ペ ポ. In much standard speech, じ/ぢ and ず/づ share a pronunciation but retain distinct conventional spellings.

きゃ きゅ きょ; しゃ しゅ しょ; ちゃ ちゅ ちょ; にゃ にゅ にょ; ひゃ ひゅ ひょ; みゃ みゅ みょ; りゃ りゅ りょ; ぎゃ ぎゅ ぎょ; じゃ じゅ じょ; びゃ びゅ びょ; ぴゃ ぴゅ ぴょ. Each combination occupies one mora. Katakana has matching combinations and additional loanword combinations such as ティ and ファ.
building: に + ほ + ん → にほん; 日本 = Japan (Nihon/Nippon depending on context). Do not assume a kanji has only one reading.
食べる → 食べます → 食べません → 食べました = eat → eat (polite) → do not eat (polite) → ate (polite). Recognise the stem and the ending.
私は日本語を勉強しています。 = I am studying Japanese. は marks the topic; を marks the object; the predicate comes at the end. Subjects can be omitted when understood.
phrases: 日本語を勉強しています。
もう一度言ってください。
この言葉はどういう意味ですか。

sections.title: Particles and topic-comment structure
sections.explanation: Japanese often places the predicate at the end and omits recoverable arguments. は frames a topic, が commonly marks a subject or focused identification, を an object, に a goal/time or other governed relation, and で a setting or means. Their functions are not one-word English translations. Contrast can make は replace or accompany certain marking. First identify the predicate, then reconstruct its arguments from context.
examples: 私は図書館で本を読みます。
I read books at the library.
は topic, で action setting, を object.
この方法が重要です。
This method is important.
が identifies the subject in this context.
exercises: Why are は and が not simply interchangeable?
They organise topic, focus and grammatical relations differently. Context and contrast affect the choice.
Identify the action setting in the first example.
図書館で. で marks where reading takes place.

sections.title: Verb forms, negation and aspect
sections.explanation: Learn verbs by conjugation class and core dictionary, negative, past and て forms. 読む becomes 読まない, 読んだ, 読んで. Polite forms such as 読みます express register. ている can mark ongoing activity or a resulting state depending on the verb: 読んでいる is reading; 結婚している is being married. Past た is not a universal completed-action marker divorced from discourse.
examples: 今、報告書を読んでいます。
I am reading the report now.
ている presents an ongoing activity.
結果はまだ分かりません。
The result is not yet known to me/us.
Polite negative; context supplies the experiencer.
exercises: Give the て-form of 書く.
書いて. It belongs to the relevant consonant-verb pattern.
Does ている always mean an action occurring now?
No. It can mark resulting states, habits and other context-dependent interpretations.

sections.title: Modifiers, clauses and formal reasoning
sections.explanation: A modifying clause normally precedes its noun without an English relative pronoun: 昨日読んだ本. Quotation and report use と; nominalisers such as こと and の turn propositions into noun-like structures with different distributions. ので often presents a reason with explanatory framing; から is also causal. Conditions と, ば, たら and なら differ in time, assumption and speaker intention.
examples: 昨日読んだ論文
the paper I read yesterday
Pre-nominal clause modifier.
条件が変われば、結果も変わります。
If conditions change, the result changes too.
ば conditional; も adds the result to the relation.
exercises: Find the head of 昨日読んだ論文.
論文. The preceding clause modifies it.
Why should four Japanese conditionals not be learned as identical if words?
Their restrictions differ for automatic consequences, future events, suppositions and decisions.

sections.title: Respect, humility and workplace language
sections.explanation: Honorific and humble expressions position people in a social relationship. 尊敬語 elevates an appropriate person's action, while 謙譲語 lowers the speaker's side in relevant relations. Polite です/ます does not cover the entire honorific system. Learn who performs each action and toward whom it is directed. A memorised respectful verb used for your own action can reverse the intended relationship.
examples: 確認していただけますか。
Could you check it for me/us?
A courteous request using an receiving-benefit structure.
担当者に確認いたします。
I will check with the person in charge.
いたす is a humble form associated with the speaker's action.
exercises: What must you identify before choosing an honorific form?
Agent, recipient, in-group/out-group relation, relationship and medium.
Write a courteous clarification request.
この点について、もう少し詳しく説明していただけますか。 A fuller explanation is requested without a blunt command.

sections.title: Professional reading and inference
sections.explanation:
Formal Japanese uses nominalisation, passive perspectives and long modifiers. Distinguish 示す show/indicate, 示唆する suggest and 証明する prove.
Teaching passage: この結果は、二つの要因の関連を示している。しかし、一方が他方の原因であることを証明しているわけではない。結論を評価する際には、調査の条件を確認する必要がある。
Translation: This result indicates an association between two factors. However, it does not mean that it proves one is the cause of the other. When evaluating the conclusion, the investigation conditions need checking.
examples: 証明しているわけではない
it does not mean that it proves ...
わけではない denies the stated interpretation, not necessarily every related possibility.
評価する際には
when evaluating
際 is a formal occasion/time noun modified by a verb.
exercises: What claim does the passage avoid?
It avoids treating association as proven causation.
Write a source summary and identify one limitation.
Preserve predicate scope, omitted referents and distinctions between evidence and interpretation.

rules.title: Topic は
rules.explanation: は marks a topic or contrast and is pronounced wa as a particle. A topic is not necessarily a grammatical subject. Japanese can omit participants understood from context.

examples.native: 彼女は無邪気なふりをした。
examples.translation: She pretended innocence.

examples.native: 私は息子に芝生に水を撒かせた。
examples.translation: I had my son water the lawn.

examples.native: 彼らはクリスマスイブに教会に行った。
examples.translation: They went to church on Christmas Eve.

rules.title: Subject and focus が
rules.explanation: が often marks a subject or focused identification. Certain predicates govern が for a participant English treats differently. It also links clauses with a contrasting meaning in another construction.

examples.native: 怒鳴りつけたかったが思いとどまった。
examples.translation: He was about to explode, but checked himself.

examples.native: オーストラリアには多くのおもしろい動物がいる。
examples.translation: There are many interesting animals in Australia.

examples.native: 仕事もたいがい片付いた。
examples.translation: Almost all the work is done now.

rules.title: Object を
rules.explanation: を commonly marks a direct object and is pronounced o. It can also mark a route or place traversed. Identify the verb’s construction rather than applying one English object rule.

examples.native: お留守中の猫の世話をして上げましょう。
examples.translation: While they are away, let's take care of their cat.

examples.native: もっと時間をかけて発表を準備すべきだったと先生に言われた。
examples.translation: My teacher told me that I should have spent more time preparing my presentation.

examples.native: ちょっと顔を貸してくれませんか。
examples.translation: Can I have a few words with you?

rules.title: に relations
rules.explanation: に marks many destinations, recipients, time points and locations with existence predicates. It is also part of other grammatical constructions. Contrast event location with で.

examples.native: パーティーに行かない。
examples.translation: I'm not going to go to the party.

examples.native: 明日買い物に行きます。
examples.translation: I'm going shopping tomorrow.

examples.native: 人からしてもらいたいように人にしてやれ。
examples.translation: Do to others as you would be done by.

rules.title: で relations
rules.explanation: で often marks event location, means or material. Compare 学校にいる, be at school, with 学校で勉強する, study at school. It can also link a noun/adjectival predicate.

examples.native: 彼は本当のところ支配人ではない。
examples.translation: He is actually not the manager.

examples.native: トムね、自分で髪切ったのよ。
examples.translation: Tom cut his own hair.

examples.native: ボクシングやホッケーのようなスポーツは好きではない。
examples.translation: I don't like such sports as boxing and hockey.

rules.title: Possession and modification の
rules.explanation: の links nouns in many relationships, including possession. It can also nominalise a clause. The relation is broader than English possessive ’s.

examples.native: 彼女の友達は歌手です。
examples.translation: Her friend is a singer.

examples.native: これまた政府の隠ぺい策のようです。
examples.translation: This looks like another government cover-up.

examples.native: 君の場合は例外としよう。
examples.translation: We will make an exception of your case.

rules.title: Quotation and accompaniment と
rules.explanation: と links an exhaustive noun list, marks accompaniment, quotes content and occurs in a conditional pattern. Its role depends on what follows.

examples.native: 彼は全く不可能だと言った。
examples.translation: He said it was out of the question.

examples.native: 暑いと牛乳はすぐに腐る。
examples.translation: Milk does not keep long on a hot day.

examples.native: マリーゴールドは太陽とともに起きる。
examples.translation: The marigold rises with the sun.

rules.title: Inclusion も
rules.explanation: も often means also/even and replaces or combines with another marker. In negative quantity expressions it can help convey not even/none. The scope is set by the phrase it follows.

examples.native: 金は鉄よりも貴重だ。
examples.translation: Gold is more precious than iron.

examples.native: 街はクリスマスムード一色・・・もうじきイブだ。
examples.translation: The streets are in full Christmas mode - it's almost Christmas Eve.

examples.native: 友達に２０年も会ってない。
examples.translation: I hadn't seen my friend for over twenty years.

rules.title: Polite present ending
rules.explanation: ます marks a polite affirmative non-past predicate. Japanese non-past covers present habits and many future contexts. Attach it to the appropriate verb stem, not the dictionary form unchanged.

examples.native: 食事ですよ。今、いきます。
examples.translation: Dinner's ready. I'm coming.

examples.native: 列車は時刻通りに出ますか。
examples.translation: Will the train leave on time?

examples.native: 私は東京までの往復券を持っています。
examples.translation: I have a round trip ticket to Tokyo.

rules.title: Polite past ending
rules.explanation: ました marks a polite affirmative past form. Recognise the verb stem and preceding complements before converting a sentence to past.

examples.native: ガソリンスタンドを探しましょう。燃料がなくなってしまいました。
examples.translation: Let's find a gas station; we've run out of fuel.

examples.native: こつが飲み込めましたか。
examples.translation: Got the hang of it?

examples.native: 私は遊ぶために公園へ行きました。
examples.translation: I went to the park to play.

rules.title: Polite negation
rules.explanation: ません marks a polite non-past negative. Past polite negative commonly uses ませんでした. The negative form also participates in some invitations/questions.

examples.native: 彼女は私にお金を返してくれませんでした。
examples.translation: She didn't give me my money back.

examples.native: 駅までの行き方を教えていただけませんか。
examples.translation: Could you tell me how to get to the station?

examples.native: 抜歯しなければなりません。
examples.translation: Your tooth must be extracted.

rules.title: Plain negation
rules.explanation: Plain negative verbs commonly end in ない with class-dependent stem changes. Some adjectives and copulas have their own negative constructions. Do not attach ない indiscriminately to every dictionary form.

examples.native: 私をどなり散らす人は気にならないわ。
examples.translation: The ones who shout at me don't bother me.

examples.native: そのなぞなぞの解き方が解らない。
examples.translation: I can't figure out how to solve the puzzle.

examples.native: なんで傘さしてんの？ 雨降ってないよ。
examples.translation: Why do you have your umbrella up? It's not raining.

rules.title: Te-form links and requests
rules.pattern: (?:てください|でください|ている|でいる|ています|でいます)
rules.explanation: The te-form joins predicates and builds constructions such as requests and いる aspect. The stem change depends on verb class. ている can mark an ongoing action or a resulting state.

examples.native: 私はあなたのぐちには死ぬほどうんざりしている。
examples.translation: I am sick to death of your complaints.

examples.native: 君の成功は主に好機をいかにして上手に利用するかにかかっている。
examples.translation: Your success will largely depend upon how you will make good use of your opportunity.

examples.native: 外交官には様々な特権が与えられている。
examples.translation: Diplomats are allowed various privileges.

rules.title: Plain past and experience
rules.explanation: A past form plus ことがある expresses experience. A past verb also modifies a noun directly. The construction as a whole determines the reading; the ending alone does not establish experience.

examples.native: これ見たことある？
examples.translation: Have you seen this?

examples.native: 彼は涙を流したことがはずかしかった。
examples.translation: He was ashamed of his tears.

examples.native: お返事が遅れたことをお許し下さい。
examples.translation: Excuse me for not having answered your letter sooner.

rules.title: Cause
rules.explanation: から and ので can supply reasons. から also marks a source/start point. Degree of explicitness and discourse tone differ between causal expressions.

examples.native: 彼は窓から出て行った。
examples.translation: He went out the window.

examples.native: 月は地球から遠い。
examples.translation: The moon is distant from the earth.

examples.native: 私はただ休養したいのです。
examples.translation: I just want to rest.

rules.title: Contrast and concession
rules.pattern: (?:けど|けれど|しかし|のに|でも)
rules.explanation: These forms connect contrast or concession but differ in grammar and register. のに presents a contrary-to-expectation relation. でも has additional functions, including examples and alternatives.

examples.native: 少女は友達にお茶をいれるのに忙しかった。
examples.translation: The girl was busy making tea for her friend.

examples.native: 彼が話をやめるように頼んだが、彼はそれでもはなしつづけた。
examples.translation: I asked him to stop talking, but he still went on.

examples.native: 博物館は月曜日が休館だって言われたけどな。
examples.translation: I've been told that the museum is closed on Mondays.

rules.title: Conditions
rules.explanation: Japanese has several condition constructions with different timing and assumptions. もし can flag an if scenario but does not replace the needed predicate form. Avoid treating と, ば, たら and なら as fully interchangeable.

examples.native: 長い目で見れば、正直は報われる。
examples.translation: Honesty pays in the long run.

examples.native: 「もしも僕が豚になっても、変わらず友達でいてくれる？」「もちろんだよ！」
examples.translation: 'Would you still be my friend even if I turned into a pig all of a sudden?' 'Of course!'

examples.native: 今、あなたがパソコンの電源を切れば、地球温暖化防止に貢献できる。
examples.translation: If you turned off your computer right now, you would contribute to the prevention of global warming.

rules.title: Nominalisation and explanation
rules.explanation: こと can nominalise a proposition/activity. のです/んです adds explanatory framing. A nominalised clause can itself take particles and play a noun-like role.

examples.native: これ、本当にノンアルコールビールなんですか？
examples.translation: Is this really a non-alcoholic beer?

examples.native: 大統領は発展途上諸国に十分な援助を提供することを決めた。
examples.translation: The President decided to provide developing countries with sufficient aid.

examples.native: 最初は彼のことを信じなかった。
examples.translation: I didn't believe him at first.

rules.title: Polite requests
rules.pattern: (?:お願いします|ください|いただけ|いただき|いらっしゃ)
rules.explanation: Politeness depends on the entire construction and social relationship. Honorific and humble forms orient differently to whose action is described; they are not merely longer synonyms.

examples.native: 知らせてください。
examples.translation: Please let me know.

examples.native: 私にお茶を入れてください。
examples.translation: Please make me some tea.

examples.native: 水分をたくさん取ってください。
examples.translation: You should drink a lot of liquid.

rules.title: Questions and stance
rules.pattern: (?:か|でしょう|かもしれない|と思う)
rules.explanation: か can mark a question or embed one; でしょう and かもしれない express stance at different strengths. A cautious inference does not have the same force as a factual assertion.

examples.native: 現在はどちらにお住まいですか。
examples.translation: Where do you live now?

examples.native: 風呂場はどこですか。
examples.translation: Where is the bathroom?

examples.native: ジュディは明日日本について話をするでしょう。
examples.translation: Judy will talk about Japan tomorrow.

passages.title: Learning with a clear purpose
passages.native: 新しい言語を勉強しています。毎日、短い文章を読んで、分かりやすい例を聞きます。役に立つ単語をノートに書きます。間違えたら、文法のルールを確認して、もう一度やってみます。目標は、人の話を理解し、自分の考えをはっきり伝えることです。
passages.translation: I am learning a new language. Each day, I read a short text and listen to clear examples. I write useful words in a notebook. When I make a mistake, I check the rule and try again. My goal is to understand people and express my ideas clearly.

grammarTerms: Noun
A word naming a person, thing or idea: student, book, freedom.
Verb
A word describing an action or state: read, know, be.
Subject
The participant linked to the main verb’s subject pattern. In The student reads a book, the student is the subject.
Object
A participant selected by a verb. In The student reads a book, a book is the direct object.
Agreement
One word changes to match another, for example an adjective matching a noun’s gender and number.
Case
A noun/pronoun form marking its relationship in a sentence. Cases can mark subjects, objects, possession or relations usually expressed by English prepositions.
Gender
A grammatical noun class. It does not always describe the sex of a person or any physical property.
Tense
A verb system that relates a situation to a time, often past or non-past.
Aspect
How a situation is viewed: unfolding, completed, habitual, experienced or in a resulting state.
Infinitive
A non-finite verb form often used for a dictionary entry or a complement. It does not by itself give the ordinary person/tense pattern.
Participle
A verb-derived form used in compound predicates or as a modifier; its exact function depends on the language and construction.
Clause
A unit organised around a predicate. One sentence can contain several clauses.
Register
Language choices suited to a situation: casual conversation, polite requests, academic writing or another context.
